Communicating with diverse audiences effectively is an important part of any communications strategy. In California, public-sector communicators face the unique challenge of sharing information on often complex topics and issues with numerous stakeholder groups. Join Liselle DeGrave, APR, president of DeGrave Communications, Inc., to learn how you can successfully develop communications strategies to engage multiple audiences on any budget. During this webinar, Liselle will share a case study of the recent tri-county (Orange, Riverside and San Bernardino counties) Trust the Tap campaign. Key takeaways from this hands-on course include:. * How to research community demographics and other important information. * How to gain insight into beliefs and perceptions of target audiences. * How to engage effectively pitch stories to non-English media. * How to successfully work with partnering agencies on a large project. * How to create an outreach strategy and tactical roadmap. * Lessons learned, tips and tools. **Speaker:** Liselle DeGrave, APR, Owner/President of DeGrave Communications. ##### ABOUT LISELLE. A veteran public-sector communications professional and business owner, Liselle has more than 15 years of experience developing effective, award-winning strategic communications programs and projects for numerous water agencies and cities throughout California. Her specialties include strategic planning, media relations, multi-cultural and community relations and engagement, special events, content creation and digital communications. Liselle has also served on the board for the California Water Awareness Campaign, was the publicity chair for the City of Murrieta Fire Auxiliary and is currently assembly delegate for the Public Relations Society of America Inland Empire Chapter board of directors. She is bilingual in English and Spanish and has used this skill set to conduct outreach diverse outreach campaigns for several water agencies as well as national campaigns for the Centers for Disease Control and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Liselle graduated from San Diego State University with Bachelors in Communications Studies: emphasis in public relations, minor in Spanish. results.title: Maximizing Impact: Effective Strategies for Research Dissemination After Publication
results.content: In academic research, dissemination refers to the process of distributing and communicating research findings to a broader audience beyond the academic community. Dissemination aims to ensure that research findings are accessible, understandable, and usable by these diverse audiences. Using dissemination strategies to encourage the active involvement of the public and other target audiences inevitably boosts the societal impact of your research. * Active dissemination strategies use specific techniques and communication channels to spread evidence-based information to a targeted audience, such as offering a guide for replication. The success of your research dissemination depends significantly on identifying and targeting the right audiences. As you can see, identifying and understanding your target audience is crucial for effective research dissemination. Effectively communicating with your target audience requires choosing the best methods for research dissemination. To reach the right people and achieve the desired impact, you must thoughtfully select the dissemination methods that reflect the audience’s preferences as well as your own research goals.

results.title: Effective Strategies for Research Dissemination and Outreach
results.content:
Title: Effective Strategies for Research Dissemination and Outreach
Effective Strategies for Research Dissemination and Outreach. Moreover, when research findings are disseminated effectively, they can inform public policy, drive innovation, and contribute to societal well-being. By employing these strategies, researchers can ensure that their work reaches diverse audiences, fostering a culture of knowledge sharing and collaborative growth. Public presentations serve as a vital conduit for research dissemination, bridging the gap between complex research findings and a broader, often non-specialist audience. In summary, public presentations are a powerful method for research dissemination that, when executed effectively, can demystify complex findings and engage a diverse audience. Engaging with traditional media remains a cornerstone strategy for researchers aiming to broaden the reach and impact of their findings. Social media has emerged as a pivotal tool in the realm of research dissemination, offering unparalleled opportunities to share findings with a broader audience. One of the key advantages of using social media for research dissemination is the potential for real-time engagement. By leveraging the power of social media, researchers can ensure that their work reaches a wider, more varied audience, ultimately enhancing the impact and relevance of their research. Community outreach events serve as pivotal platforms for disseminating research findings and fostering local engagement. Ultimately, community outreach events are more than just a means to disseminate research findings; they are opportunities to build lasting relationships between researchers and the community. Assessing the effectiveness of dissemination and outreach strategies is crucial for ensuring that research findings reach the intended audience and achieve the desired impact. By systematically evaluating and refining dissemination strategies, researchers can enhance their ability to communicate complex findings, ultimately contributing to the advancement of knowledge and societal progress. In the realm of academic research, the dissemination and outreach of findings are pivotal for fostering knowledge transfer and societal impact. To achieve this, researchers must adhere to several best practices that encapsulate clear communication, strategic audience engagement, and continuous evaluation of their dissemination efforts. Researchers should strive to present their findings in a manner that is both accessible and engaging to a diverse audience. Embracing these best practices will empower researchers to effectively disseminate their work, fostering a culture of open, impactful, and engaged research dissemination.
